clue.text: Infant born during recess

indicators.note: something happening during a period sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a bay is a recess in a wall or room
b. is the standard abbreviation for born

explanation.surface: A child arrives while Parliament is in its holiday recess.
explanation.walkthrough: BAY wraps around B.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is a very young child, which is exactly what an infant is: a direct synonym.

clue.text: Body of troops ordered to capture equipment

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one piece is put around another

blocks.note: bade is the past tense of bid, meaning ordered or commanded
rig is gear or apparatus

explanation.surface: Soldiers are commanded to seize enemy kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as the troops being arranged in ranks; here it is the old past tense of bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigade is a military unit made up of several battalions, so it is a body of troops.

clue.text: Something for the beach, a bit much? Gent so embarrassed

indicators.note: an embarrassed person is flustered and thrown into disarray, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: all fourteen letters taken as fodder

explanation.surface: A gentleman blushes at a skimpy swimsuit on the beach, finding it a bit much.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathing costume is a swimsuit, worn at the seaside: a deliberately vague description of an item for the beach.

clue.text: Passionate tale involving maiden

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece is enclosed by another

blocks.note: a story is a tale
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A romance novel about a young woman, full of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: STORY takes in M: STOR(M)Y. M for maiden comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: A stormy relationship or temperament is fiery and emotionally intense, a figurative synonym for passionate.

clue.text: Move by one knight to intervene

blocks.note: a step is a move
Roman numeral one
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A chess player advances a single knight to block an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To step in is the idiom for getting involved in a situation, the phrasal-verb equivalent of intervene.

clue.text: Boy let us out, dim-wittedly

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or not in order, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: eight letters taken as fodder

explanation.surface: A lad foolishly releases someone, perhaps from a locked room.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand, so acting obtusely is acting in a stupid, slow-witted manner.

clue.text: Motive, primarily, behind very short note

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of that word is kept
behind means coming after, so this piece is placed at the end

blocks.note: mini is a prefix or word meaning very small or short
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A musician's reason sits behind a very brief note.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'M behind MINI', so MINI comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note worth half a semibreve, known in American usage as a half note.

clue.text: Was king around end of thirties - abdicated

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept
around means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped about the other

blocks.note: a king reigns, so 'was king' is reigned
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A monarch who ruled until the late 1930s gave up the throne, as Edward VIII did in 1936.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to Edward VIII, who abdicated in December 1936, so 'end of thirties' fits the history as well as the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Abdicating is formally giving up an office, so resigned is a synonym for it.

clue.text: Constable, perhaps, getting results with tricks used in picture-making

blocks.note: a special constable is a volunteer police officer in Britain, often just called a special
effects are results; 'getting' joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A painter like John Constable achieves striking results with tricks of the trade.
explanation.walkthrough: Constable seems to be the landscape painter, which fits 'picture-making'; it is the police rank. A special is an unpaid British part-time police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Special effects are the illusions and visual trickery used in films, which are motion pictures.

clue.text: Very unpleasant smell coming from tail of cartilaginous fish

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: last letter of the word
the tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A rotten fish such as a shark or ray gives off a foul odour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cartilaginous fish' reads as one phrase, but only its last letter is used before a separate fish; the tench is bony anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong, foul odour, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Undergoing a state of transition at home, plotting changes involving text

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the extra word goes inside the fodder
changes means alters, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: in means at home
taken as written
a text can mean the subject or theme of a sermon or discussion

explanation.surface: Someone at home scheming over a document is going through a period of change.
explanation.walkthrough: A text can be the subject a preacher expounds, hence a theme; that word sits inside the fodder before the whole is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in the melting pot is the idiom for being in flux, with its outcome still undecided.

clue.text: Draws on novel alibi to reveal talents

indicators.note: novel means new, so the word following it is made anew in a fresh order
on means attached after, so the first piece is joined after the second

blocks.note: five letters taken as fodder
a tie is a drawn match

explanation.surface: A writer draws on an original alibi to show off their gifts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draws on' looks like 'makes use of', but draws are TIES placed on the rearranged alibi.
explanation.definitionFit: Abilities are skills or aptitudes, a direct synonym for talents.

clue.text: A bit of cork in my French wine

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece of it, here its opening letter
in places the preceding pieces inside the next one

blocks.note: mon is French for my
taken as written
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fragment of cork has fallen into a Frenchman's glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' reads as an adjective for the wine but belongs with 'my', and the clue's opening 'A' is a letter in its own right.
explanation.definitionFit: Mâcon is a wine from the Mâconnais district of southern Burgundy, so it is an example of a wine.

clue.text: English home with electronic source of power

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for English
in means at home
e is the prefix for electronic, as in e-mail; 'with' joins it on

explanation.surface: A house in England fitted with modern electrical power.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine is a machine that converts energy into motion, so it drives and powers a vehicle or device.

clue.text: Messy hit and run

blocks.note: to slap is to hit
to dash is to run; 'and' joins the pieces

explanation.surface: A messy hit-and-run incident on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash describes work done hastily and carelessly, which leaves it untidy.

clue.text: You'd think you'd find alligators on one, but you won't!

definitions.text: You'd think you'd find alligators on one, but you won't!

blocks.clueFragment: You'd think you'd find alligators on one, but you won't!
blocks.note: surface reading: a joke about where reptiles might be found
setter's reading: alligator pear is an old name for the avocado, which grows on a different tree from the one its name suggests

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about where you might expect to see alligators.
explanation.walkthrough: Alligator pear is another name for the avocado; by its name it should grow on the fruit tree in the answer, but it does not.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree named in the answer bears pears, yet alligator pears, being avocados, grow elsewhere.

clue.text: Overlooking man, Batman and Robin foolishly talk at length

indicators.note: overlooking means ignoring, so the named word is left out
foolishly suggests disorder, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: the superhero's name
the word to drop from the superhero's name
his sidekick, joined by 'and'

explanation.surface: Batman and Robin behaving foolishly while ignoring some man.
explanation.walkthrough: BATMAN loses MAN to leave BAT, which is mixed with ROBIN. To rabbit on is British slang for chattering endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbit on is British informal for talking at tedious length, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk.

clue.text: General behaviour in a Manhattan street

blocks.note: broad means general, as in broad terms
one's ways are one's behaviour

explanation.surface: An army general's conduct while walking the streets of New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like a military rank but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadway is the long avenue running through Manhattan, famous for its theatres.

clue.text: Cut and dry in brief space of time

indicators.note: in places the word before it inside the following piece

blocks.note: a bit is a short while, as in 'wait a bit'
sec is French for dry, used of wines

explanation.surface: Something trimmed and dried out in no time at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Sec on a wine label means dry, which is why the French word stands for it here.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut into two equal parts, a specific kind of cutting.

clue.text: Crime writer's killers left out

indicators.note: out means removed, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: slayers are killers
L is the abbreviation for left, the letter dropped

explanation.surface: A detective novelist's murderers have been omitted from the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L. Sayers wrote detective novels featuring Lord Peter Wimsey, so she is an example of a crime writer.

clue.text: Joins privates after one drops out

indicators.note: something that drops out leaves, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: privates are ordinary soldiers
Roman numeral one, the letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone enlists in the army after a recruit quits.
explanation.definitionFit: To solder is to join metal parts with melted alloy, so solders is a specific way of joining.

clue.text: Boy in game, forward

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
forward means cheeky or bold, which is pert

explanation.surface: A lad playing in a match as a forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward' suggests a rugby position, but it is the adjective meaning impudent.
explanation.definitionFit: Rupert is a male first name, so it is an example of a boy's name, as crosswords often use.

clue.text: Attack head of sixth-form college

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: first letter of the word
Eton College is the famous English boarding school

explanation.surface: Someone assaults the headteacher of a school's sixth form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of sixth-form college' reads as a headteacher; it is S plus ETON. The sixth form is the final two years of an English secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: To set on someone is to attack them, as in 'set on by thugs'.

clue.text: Dapper, some aldermen at Tynwald

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: inside letters 8-12 of 'aldermen at Tynwald'

explanation.surface: Smartly dressed councillors at the Isle of Man's parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Tynwald is the parliament of the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Natty means smart and neatly dressed, a direct synonym for dapper.

clue.text: Available in large quantities where Carrie Watts grew up

blocks.note: first meaning: plentiful, abundant
second meaning: the Texas town she longs to revisit in Horton Foote's play and film The Trip to ...

explanation.walkthrough: Carrie Watts is the elderly heroine of The Trip to Bountiful, who sets off to see her childhood hometown.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means plentiful and is also the name of the fictional Texas town in Foote's story.

clue.text: Deliver free

blocks.note: first meaning: save someone from danger
second meaning: release someone from a predicament

explanation.walkthrough: 'Deliver free' looks like a shop's postage offer; both words are verbs meaning rescue.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming to someone's rescue means saving or liberating them, as in 'deliver us from evil'.

clue.text: Type of ring, reportedly for a young bird

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the answer matches the spoken form

blocks.note: a signet ring bears a seal or crest

explanation.surface: A ring said to be meant for a fledgling.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, so it is an example of a young bird.

clue.text: River goddess

blocks.note: first meaning: the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford
second meaning: the Egyptian goddess of magic and motherhood

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a single river goddess, but these are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isis is the stretch of the Thames at Oxford, and Isis was a major Egyptian deity.
